pillar: Reducing the cost of building AI systems
title: CRUCIBLE
description: A multi-agent framework for calibrating annotation rubrics through iterative diagnosis of disagreement between LLM judges. Accepted at ATRACC, AAAI Fall Symposium Series 2026; camera-ready submitted. Code and evaluation artifacts are available in the repository.

pillar: Enabling AI to run outside centralized infrastructure
title: SNR-Detector
description: A binary classification framework for distinguishing signal from noise in educational video transcripts using embeddings and a lightweight classifier. The research manuscript is available as an SSRN preprint; code and evaluation artifacts are public.

title: Essence
description: Research on peer-isolated personalization: when an individual user’s own history is sufficient for recommendation, and when collaborative signals help. The longer-term aim is to capture a listener’s subjective emotional experience. Accepted at NewInML, NeurIPS 2026 (non-archival); an expanded controlled study is accepted at SOICT 2026.

title: Asterism
description: A local-first, Hebbian-weighted knowledge graph that acts as a priority index over long-term LLM memory without model fine-tuning. Accepted at NORA, AACL-IJCNLP 2026; camera-ready submitted. Storage is local; external model calls depend on the chosen backend.

pillar: Evaluating the limits of LLM agents
title: Symbolic Grounding & Conformity
description: A pre-registered investigation of whether symbolic grounding protects LLM agents against conformity, reporting a null result and a benchmark-saturation obstacle. Accepted for presentation at NeSyDebates, KSE 2026; the remote presentation route is non-archival.
